item.title: Govt plans colour-coded DLs for Indians, foreigners; may scrap affidavits
item.description: Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposing sweeping changes to the driving licence (DL) regime under Motor Vehicles Rules, the road transport ministry Wednesday issued a draft notification to raise the pass mark for the online safe-driving tutorial assessment from the current 60% to 75%.
item.dc:creator: DIPAK K DASH

item.title: ‘Ridiculed for eating beef’ at school, 16-year-old Tamil Nadu boy dies by suicide
item.description: In Coimbatore, a tragic incident unfolded as 16-year-old A Akilan, a Scheduled Caste student, took his own life allegedly due to persistent harassment from peers and a teacher over his dietary preferences. His mother highlighted that repeated pleas to school officials were ignored, resulting in this heartbreaking event. Authorities have initiated a case against the teacher, headmaster, and two students, inciting public protests for justice and a thorough investigation.
item.dc:creator: TYSION PRABHU

item.title: Texas farmer went from 27 sheep to overseeing 10,000 across 40,000 acres
item.description: JR Howard experienced hardships early on with only a small number of sheep, making it tough to earn a living. However, after landing a grazing contract with solar farms, he expanded his flock and income significantly. This eco-friendly grazing method is being embraced by renewable energy companies as a cost-effective way to manage vegetation, while farmers benefit from expansive grazing land without hefty property expenses.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Elon Musk responds to statement that he may be in jail soon
item.description: Elon Musk recently addressed journalist Kara Swisher's caution regarding possible investigations into his various enterprises. Swisher noted that if Democrats regain control of Congress in upcoming elections, probes could restart. Additionally, she implied that Musk's political ties might shield him from scrutiny. Bernie Sanders has voiced his disapproval of Musk's extensive political expenditures, underscoring the risks of oligarchs meddling in the democratic process.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Ontario farmer turned down C$16m for 164 acres; 29 acres protected for 999 years
item.description: Charles Stevens and his family have decided to protect Wilmot Orchards by placing a conservation easement on the property. This easement effectively restricts future development for nearly 1,000 years, ensuring continued agricultural use. Their decision counters pressures from developers seeking to convert farmland into housing. The Stevens family aims to preserve the land for future generations of farmers.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Can Kimi Antonelli clinch the F1 2026 title in Austin?
item.description: Kimi Antonelli heads to the United States Grand Prix in Austin with a 102-point lead in the 2026 Formula 1 championship. With six races remaining, the Mercedes youngster could move closer to becoming the youngest world champion in F1 history. George Russell, Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen remain mathematically in contention, but Antonelli's title hopes could receive a decisive boost if results go his way in Texas.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: 'Lifting sanctions will make Putin stronger': Zelenskyy differs with Trump on Russia
item.dc:creator: ABHISHEK MISHRA

item.title: Only ‘sanatanis’ will touch Durga idols during immersion: Bengal CM Suvendu
item.description: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that only those who believe in Sanatan Dharma can touch Durga idols during immersion. This directive aims to maintain the sanctity of traditional rituals amidst rising political tensions. Several opposition leaders criticized the decision, alleging it promotes religious exclusion and violates constitutional principles. The immersion involved the use of trolleys instead of cranes, which is a departure from previous practices.
item.dc:creator: SAIKAT RAY, KRISHNENDU BANDYOPADHYAY, KAUSHIK PRADHAN

item.title: Rare steel watch estimated at $240,000 sells for $1.016m in New York
item.description: At a recent Phillips auction, an exquisite stainless-steel timepiece crafted by renowned watchmaker Kari Voutilainen commanded an impressive $1.016 million, far surpassing its estimated value. The Voutilainen 28Sport Limited Edition features a stunning blue guilloché dial complemented by a striking black onyx center. Originally acquired in 2021, this watch's sale underscores the increasing allure of exceptional and rare watches within the collector community.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Portland man spent $48,412 on backyard; rentals brought in $85,000 by 2025
item.description: Rob Nachbar skillfully turned his once-simple backyard in Portland into a thriving rental space known as Pong Springs. This five-year renovation, which cost $48,412, prioritized weather-resistant structures and enhanced privacy features. Since its launch on Swimply, Nachbar has generated approximately $106,000 in revenue. The yard not only hosts various events but also provides the family with a serene private retreat—combining leisure and financial success.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean
item.description: President Trump has recently proposed renaming the Atlantic Ocean, following prior discussions about the Atlantic Ocean. During a recent event, he mentioned contacting Google Maps regarding these renaming efforts. Google CEO Sundar Pichai reportedly declined his proposal on the grounds that oceans encompass multiple countries. This follows the US administration's earlier renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Why children look at the world between their legs, according to psychology
item.description: When children bend forward to peer between their legs, they unveil a fresh perspective on their surroundings. This playful curiosity is fueled by an innate desire to discover and understand the world visually. Developmental psychology highlights that this behavior is linked to enjoyment and the social dynamics around them. Parents should embrace these explorations as part of ordinary growth, without overreacting or worrying unduly.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: California family spent $4,000 turning its front yard into Jurassic Park
item.description: In Granada Hills, a family has dedicated $4,000 to create an elaborate Jurassic Park-themed display for Halloween. After investing over 200 hours, they've constructed life-sized dinosaur replicas and an automated escape show, complete with grand entrance gates. Open to the public at no cost, this attraction fosters community spirit as neighbors flock to capture the experience and enjoy this festive installation.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Jason Momoa buys Sam Neill's former 4.92-hectare NZ estate for NZ$15m
item.description: Jason Momoa has recently acquired a significant property in Queenstown, New Zealand for NZ$15 million. The estate, formerly owned by Sir Sam Neill, demonstrates the increasing interest in the local real estate market. Property values in the region have risen significantly, attracting overseas buyers. Momoa has deep connections to New Zealand, having visited frequently for leisure and work. He has also invested in the local film industry and nightlife scene.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Virginia teen's model improves simulated earthquake sensor coverage by 16.7%
item.description: A 14-year-old student from Williamsburg, Virginia, has become one of 30 finalists in a national science competition after developing a mathematical model to improve earthquake sensor placement. Isabel Rossi's six-month research project showed that adding just five sensors could increase simulated detection coverage by 16.7%. She used earthquake records from California and mathematical methods to identify better sensor locations.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Red Corner Notice against Russian ‘who fled with child’
item.description: The Delhi Police have issued a Red Corner Notice for Russian citizen Viktoriia Basu due to alleged violations of child custody regulations. Viktoriia reportedly exited India with her son in defiance of a Supreme Court shared custody ruling. Extradition efforts are currently underway with Russian officials to find her. Furthermore, an associate, Natasha, is being investigated for allegedly facilitating her departure.
item.dc:creator: KOUSHIKI SAHA

item.title: Will decide on any notice to remove CEC according to rules: LS Speaker Om Birla
item.description: Both the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha chairman had rejected previous notices from the opposition, saying their allegations “do not prima facie meet the high constitutional bar for removal proceedings”. Birla noted the process for removal of the chief election commissioner was the same as for removing a Supreme Court judge.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
item.description: Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them. Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed
item.dc:creator: SHILPA PHADNIS

item.title: Hospitals ‘overcharging’ is a malpractice: Govt to Supreme Court
item.description: In an affidavit filed in SC on the issue of capping prices of all medicines and medical consumables, chemicals and fertilisers ministry said that patients have a very low bargaining position with respect to hospitals, resulting in various malpractices. The affidavit noted the irony of India being home to companies making cheap drugs but patients here having to pay way above the manufacturing price, as well as patients being subjected to overcharging by hospitals.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: Amid attacks, sales surge at Kolkata Left bookstalls
item.description: Book stalls set up by Left parties saw significant sales increases during Durga Puja amid incidents of vandalism. The CPM stall at Jadavpur 8B bus stand recorded sales of Rs 16 lakh, nearly four times last year's figures. Despite attacks, sales for other Left stalls also increased, evidencing a broader engagement with literature. Politicians from various parties expressed solidarity with the Left stalls amidst ongoing disputes.
item.dc:creator: DIPAWALI MITRA AND POULAMI ROY

item.title: Anahat scripts history, storms into maiden PSA Gold semi-final
item.description: Anahat Singh pulled off an impressive comeback against Salma Hany, clinching her spot in the semi-finals at a PSA Gold-level event after a nail-biting five-game match that lasted 42 minutes. The 18-year-old, facing a 1-2 deficit, demonstrated resilience and skill. Anahat will now go head-to-head with Malaysia's Sivasangari Subramaniam, reigniting their rivalry from the Asian Games final, solidifying her remarkable tournament journey in Redwood City.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: Centre betrayed us, now want full statehood for Ladakh: Sonam Wangchuk
item.description: Wangchuk said the representatives of Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) had come prepared for Oct 22 talks in Delhi as a follow up of the May 15 meeting in Leh, with the expectation that the MHA and Ladakh bodies' respective drafts on contours and powers of UT-level body and district councils, would be discussed.
item.dc:creator: BHARTI JAIN AND NASEER GANAI

item.title: Will back all meaningful efforts for Ukraine peace, PM Modi assures Poland's Tusk
item.description: PM Modi and his Polish counterpart Tusk expressed deepest concern in a joint statement over the war in Ukraine, including its tragic humanitarian consequences and the impact on Global South. In his media statement, Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Congress defaming India to shield Nehru-Gandhi family: PM Modi
item.description: “Dimagi naxals have captured Congress so much that it has lost its ability to think. Those who used to cause destruction in forests are now determined to wreak havoc on the country through Congress,” PM Modi said, referring to hardcore Left elements accused of being sympathetic to Maoists and now vocal in protests against EC and govt.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: 'He put it back': Trump says Ukraine's Starlink restored, stays silent on Musk
item.description: Ukraine depends heavily on Starlink for communications between military units, coordinating operations and receiving early warnings during Russian missile attacks. The satellite-based network also supports the use of drones, which Ukraine deploys both to strike Russian targets and to defend against incoming attacks. Disruptions to connectivity can therefore affect the military's ability to operate drones and respond to Russian assaults.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Tom Brady donated $170,000 Salem State speaking fee to charities in 2015
item.description: Tom Brady collected $170,000 for a speaking gig at Salem State University, generously donating the entire sum to charity. He allocated $50,000 to Best Buddies and distributed the remaining funds to various other organizations. With approximately 4,000 attendees present, ticket sales effectively covered his speaking fee. However, the event was notable for Brady facing questions about the NFL's Deflategate saga. The university reported a financial profit from hosting the event.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Movie glorifies violence, generalises graft in medical field: IMA
item.description: In a letter, dated Oct 22, to I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak sought an impartial review of the promo video for the upcoming film and appropriate corrective measures from its makers. It also called for a ban or other action if justified under applicable law. The letter was also copied to the Union health and home ministries and the chairperson of National Medical Commission.
item.dc:creator: ANUJA JAISWAL

item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo reportedly invested $70 million in real estate in 2025
item.description: Since October 2025, NBA superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo has strategically invested approximately $70 million in various real estate ventures. His family's company, Ante, has facilitated several significant purchases, including apartment complexes in Wisconsin, Brooklyn, and Chicago. Notably, he recently acquired a lavish $13.5 million mansion in Pinecrest, Florida, after joining the Miami Heat. These investments reflect Antetokounmpo's commitment to expanding his financial portfolio beyond basketball income.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Murray’s wife Kim Sears, four children: Inside his family life after retirement
item.description: Andy Murray has officially retired from professional tennis and, in doing so, has opened a new chapter in his life, and the former world No 1 will have more time to spend with his wife Kim Sears and their four children. From parenting and family routines to their shared business interests at Cromlix, the couple are handling life outside the demands of professional tennis while keeping family at the center.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: 'Keep it up': Trump backs Ramaswamy's attack ad against Ohio rival
item.description: In his post, Trump did not directly address the allegations of abuse but attacked Acton, writing: "I suggested, on the other hand, that Vivek should keep it up, and let everyone listen to the mother of a defective, dishonest, and incapable Candidate, explain how the daughter is a DISASTER who, uncontrollably, lies, cheats, and steals!"
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: In call with Bibi, PM Modi says urgent need to restore West Asia peace
item.description: PM Modi said he had received acall from Netanyahu during which the leaders reviewed the sustained momentum in bilateral ties and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the partnership. Modi did not mention Netanyahu’s invitation in his post on the conversation. “We exchanged views on developments in West Asia and underscored the urgent need to restore peace and stability in the region,” Modi said on X.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Resignation by Justice Yashwant Varma may end Lok Sabha proceedings
item.description: Justice Yashwant Varma’s name still figuring on the list of judges on the HC website had bolstered the view. However, sources said legal opinion, backed by a court verdict, that an HC judge’s resignation comes into effect as soon as he resigns may prevail in what was earlier seen as a legal grey area.
item.dc:creator: KUMAR RAKESH

item.title: Centre flags data gap, regulatory hurdles in curbing hospital mark-ups
item.description: The Union govt has told the SC in its affidavit that margins on hospital consumables can range from 100% to 1,000% or more, highlighting concerns over the high mark-ups patients often face on supplies used during treatment. However, a senior official told TOI that the govt does not have the data needed to assess margins across hospital supplies and determine whether wider controls are warranted.
item.dc:creator: ANUJA JAISWAL

item.title: MEA calls out UN report for saying Dawood Ibrahim's D-company India-based
item.description: First secretary in India’s permanent mission to UN, Raghoo Puri, was responding to a report by Ben Saul, the special rapporteur on the ‘Promotion and Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms while Countering Terrorism’. He said this presented member-states with a fait accompli, an unfortunate situation for an organisation already facing challenges to its legitimacy.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: From Jan 1, WhatsApp, Telegram won’t work without SIM cards, govt issues guidelines
item.description: The move is to curb cross-border cyber frauds, phishing, digital arrest scams using Indian mobile numbers and enhance telecom cyber security. Apple has updated iOS with a software patch to help detect when an iPhone is operating without a physical SIM card to abide with the rules. It is learnt Signal has not yet responded to govt notices.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH SINHA

item.title: Sonia Gandhi makes Instagram debut, shares first look of her upcoming book
item.description: In her first post on Instagram, Sonia shared a video of her welcoming the first copies of her autobiography “Belonging: A journey of love” which is set to be released on Nov 10. The video showed her holding up the book and then sharing sweets with daughter and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. “It is a story of love, duty, loss and finding a place to belong. I look forward to sharing it with you,” Sonia wrote on the post.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Don’t blindly follow foreign custody order: Supreme Court
item.description: A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan said cases already dealt with by foreign courts were coming before it time and again and their adjudication was not easy as they involved deeply emotional and sensitive issues. It added that the welfare of the child “must be understood in the widest sense, not by money or physical comfort alone”.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: Indian dies in Saudi airport strike; MEA slams infrastructure attacks
item.description: India has condemned the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure. “These attacks have unfortunately resulted in civilian deaths and injuries. We convey our heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family and wish speedy recovery to those injured. The Indian embassy in Riyadh...will provide all possible assistance,” said ministry of external affairs (MEA) in a statement. The victim has not been identified by Saudi authorities so far.
item.dc:creator: TNN
